### Expected behavior
Vagrant should continue as expected.

### Actual behavior

The Vagrant hanged after `netplan apply (sudo=true)`

### Steps to reproduce

I built the Ubuntu 19.10 Desktop using packer + quemu and upload it to the Vagrant Cloud.
The details about the build can be found here: https://github.com/ruzickap/packer-templates/blob/master/ubuntu-desktop.json

When I try to run `vagrant up` it got stacked at the error mentioned above.
Here is the example:

```bash
$ vagrant init peru/ubuntu-19.10-desktop-amd64-libvirt-test --box-version 0.0.1
$ VAGRANT_LOG=info vagrant up --provider=libvirt
...
...
 INFO ssh: Execute: mv -f '/tmp/vagrant-network-entry-1581002100' '/etc/netplan/50-vagrant.yaml'
chown root:root '/etc/netplan/50-vagrant.yaml'
chmod 0644 '/etc/netplan/50-vagrant.yaml'
netplan apply (sudo=true)
^C INFO interface: warn: Waiting for cleanup before exiting...
 INFO interface: warn: ==> default: Waiting for cleanup before exiting...
==> default: Waiting for cleanup before exiting...
```

If I change the `renderer = "NetworkManager"` in this file: 

https://github.com/hashicorp/vagrant/blob/master/plugins/guests/debian/cap/configure_networks.rb#L64

Everything is working file.

By default the `renderer` is set to `networkd`, but I'm not sure if it correct, because the Ubuntu Desktop is using NetworkManager.

I checked if the interface inside the guest Ubuntu VM is managed by NetworkManager (like it's here https://github.com/hashicorp/vagrant/blob/master/lib/vagrant/util/guest_inspection.rb#L91-L94) but it seems `eth0` is not:

```bash
vagrant@localhost:~$ sudo su
root@localhost:/home/vagrant# nmcli -t d show eth0 | grep unmanaged
GENERAL.STATE:10 (unmanaged)
```

-> The network of the VM itself is working fine and is accessible (via ssh), but
the main issue is that it the vagrant "up" start process is in hanged state.
comments:
From what I was able to test, the problem seems to be, that `renderer` is always used as default `NETPLAN_DEFAULT_RENDERER` (`networkd`) in https://github.com/hashicorp/vagrant/blob/master/plugins/guests/debian/cap/configure_networks.rb 

Looks like this part of code is never executed in my case:
https://github.com/hashicorp/vagrant/blob/master/plugins/guests/debian/cap/configure_networks.rb#L65-L70

```rubby
          ethernets.keys.each do |k|
            if nm_controlled?(comm, k)
              renderer = "NetworkManager"
              break
            end
          end
```

It gets never into the `ethernets.keys.each do |k|` loop to be able to change the `renderer` to `NetworkManager`. 

The `ethernets` variable is empty... which is also visible form the created `/etc/netplan/50-vagrant.yaml` file located on the guest machine:

```yaml
$ cat /etc/netplan/50-vagrant.yaml 
---
network:
  version: 2
  renderer: networkd
  ethernets: {}
```

Not sure why...

I'm hitting this issue too. 
Preseed option to remove netplan does not work `d-i netcfg/do_not_use_netplan true`.
Requires manual removal of netplan and config of networkmanager to workaround.

I commented out the netplan line on https://github.com/hashicorp/vagrant/blob/master/plugins/guests/debian/cap/configure_networks.rb#L23-L24 as a workaround.

review_comments: The `NETPLAN_DEFAULT_RENDERER` constant can be removed as well since this was the only place it was being used.

netplan supports `networkd` and `NetworkManager` as renderers (https://netplan.io/), by default it uses `networkd`. If `networkd` is not installed, Vagrant should probably fall back to `NetworkManager` if it is available. If neither of these are available, then netplan will not work (Vagrant should throw an error). 
Additionally, a device can be set to be managed by `NetworkManager`, in which case netplan should use the `NetworkManager` renderer.
